components.name: Spinner
components.description: An indeterminate loading ring in the text colour, sized like an icon. For short waits on a small area or inside a button; Skeleton covers content that's loading.

classes.ayy-spinner: The ring, 1.25em (matches an icon beside text), in the current text colour. Spins; stops still under reduced motion.

default.looks: Loading is its only look: a ring in currentColor (20% track, solid top) turning once a slow duration; under reduced motion it stops as a still ring.

hover.none: Not interactive.

pressed.none: Not interactive.

disabled.none: Not interactive.

selected.none: Not interactive.

error.none: Replace it with an Alert or FieldError when the work fails.

loading.when: always (it is the loading state); give it role="status" and a label, or aria-hidden inside a busy Button

scale.sm: 16px (--ayy-size-icon-sm).
scale.md: 1.25em, matching an icon beside text.

sizes.density: Doesn't follow data-density; md follows the font size around it.
sizes.width: Square.

components.js: spinnerClass({ size?, className? }) → string. Buttons: add aria-busy="true" and put an aria-hidden .ayy-spinner first inside (React: <Button loading>).

props.label: What's loading, for screen readers. Default "Loading" (translate it). "" makes it decorative (aria-hidden) when nearby text already says it.

a11y: A spinner on its own is a role="status" with an aria-label that says what's loading ("Loading invoices").
Inside a button, hide it (aria-hidden) and set aria-busy="true" on the button; the button's text still names it.
Mark the region that's refreshing with aria-busy="true" until the new content is in.
Under reduced motion it stops as a still ring; the label and aria-busy still say it's working.
do: Use a spinner for waits under a few seconds on a small area: a button that's saving, a panel refreshing, a lazy menu.
Put it inside the button that started the work (<Button loading>), not somewhere else on the page.
Pair a large spinner with a line of text when the wait may be longer ("Importing 2,400 contacts…").
dont: Don't use a spinner for a page or list that's loading — use Skeleton shapes of the content.
Don't use it when you know how far along the work is — use Progress.
Don't show several spinners at once; load the region as one.
Don't disable a loading button; aria-busy keeps it focusable and <Button loading> ignores repeat clicks.

components.name: Skeleton
components.description: Placeholder shapes shown while content loads, with a subtle shimmer.

classes.ayy-skeleton: Block placeholder. Set its size to match the content.

default.looks: Loading is its only look: a wash-hover block with a quiet shimmer that stops under reduced motion.

hover.none: Not interactive.

pressed.none: Not interactive.

disabled.none: Not interactive.

selected.none: Not interactive.

error.none: Replace Skeletons with an Alert and a retry when loading fails.

loading.when: always; set aria-busy="true" on the region it fills and aria-hidden on the skeletons
loading.looks: Shimmers. Forced colours: a dashed outline instead.

sizes.density: Doesn't follow data-density.
sizes.width: Size it like the content it stands in for. block fills the width at 1rem tall; text is 0.75em tall; circle is 2.5rem (an avatar).

components.js: skeletonClass({ shape?, className? }) → string
a11y: Skeletons are aria-hidden. Put aria-busy="true" on the container while loading, and remove it when content arrives. To name the loading region, give it role="status" and an aria-label — aria-label on a plain div is ignored.
The shimmer stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
do: Use a skeleton for content that takes more than ~300ms and has a predictable layout (cards, lists, profile headers).
Match the real layout closely so nothing jumps when content arrives.
dont: Don't use skeletons for unknown layouts or long jobs — use Progress.
Don't use skeletons for instant loads — skeletons that flash are worse than nothing.
Don't show skeletons for errors or empty states.

components.name: Empty state
components.description: What a list, table or page shows when there's nothing in it yet, or nothing matches: an optional icon tile, a title, one sentence on why, and the action that fills it.

classes.ayy-empty-state: Root. Centred column with generous block padding.
classes.ayy-empty-state--bordered: A dashed outline around the empty area (a board column, a drop target).
classes.ayy-empty-state--compact: Less padding: inside a card, a table body or a side panel.
classes.ayy-empty-state__title: What's empty, as a heading ("No projects yet").
classes.ayy-empty-state__description: One sentence: why it's empty, or what will appear here.
classes.ayy-empty-state__actions: The button that fixes it (primary), maybe a secondary link.

default.looks: Centred: an optional Icon tile, an lg heading-font title, a muted sm sentence (at most 42ch) and the action that fills it.

hover.none: Static; its action Buttons have their own states.

pressed.none: Not interactive.

disabled.none: Not interactive.

selected.none: Not interactive.

error.none: A failed load isn't empty: show an Alert with a retry instead.

loading.none: While loading show Skeletons, never an empty state.

sizes.density: Doesn't follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container. compact has less padding (in a card, table cell or sidebar); bordered adds a dashed card outline for an area that will hold content.

components.js: emptyStateClass({ bordered?, compact?, className? }) → string; emptyStateTitleClass, emptyStateDescriptionClass, emptyStateActionsClass constants.

react.import: import { EmptyState, EmptyStateTitle, EmptyStateDescription, EmptyStateActions } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

a11y: The title is a real heading at the level that fits the page (h2 under the page's h1, h3 inside a card).
The icon tile is decorative: the title carries the meaning.
When results change because of a search or filter, put the empty state inside a role="status" region (or announce the count) so screen reader users hear that nothing matched.
do: Use an empty state wherever a list, table or page can have nothing in it: first run, a finished inbox, a search with no results.
Say what will be here and give the one action that fills it (Create project, Import contacts, Clear filters).
Use the compact version inside a Card or a Table's body; the full one when it's the whole page.
Match the icon to the thing that's missing, in an IconTile.
dont: Don't use an empty state while data is loading — use Skeleton rows (or a Spinner for a small area).
Don't use it for errors — use an Alert with a retry action.
Don't leave a table with only headers and nothing under them.
Don't blame the user ("You haven't…"); say what's next.

components.name: Badge
components.description: Small pill label for status, category or count. Optional pulsing status dot.

components.name: Keyboard hint
components.description: A keyboard key or shortcut hint drawn as a small keycap: in help text, menus, tooltips and search fields, with platform-specific modifier adaptation (macOS ⌘/⌥, Windows Ctrl/Win, Linux Super) and international layout awareness.

classes.ayy-kbd: The <kbd>: monospace, 0.75em of the surrounding text, a hairline border with a heavier bottom edge.

default.looks: A small keycap: wash fill, line-strong border with a 2px bottom edge, mono text-soft at 0.75em.

hover.none: A key label, not a control.

pressed.none: A key label, not a control.

disabled.none: A key label, not a control.

selected.none: A key label, not a control.

error.none: No error state.

loading.none: No loading state.

sizes.width: At least 1.6em wide, grows with the key name.

components.js: kbdClass and keyboardHintClass constants. platformKeyLabel(key, platform) maps modifier names to platform symbols/names ("mod" → ⌘ on Mac, Ctrl on Windows/Linux; "meta" → ⌘ on Mac, Win on Windows, Super on Linux); platformKeyName(key, platform) gives its spoken name ("Command" for ⌘).

props.keyName: string — a modifier or key drawn for the platform ("mod", "meta", "alt", "ctrl", "shift", "enter", "backspace"). Symbols get an aria-label with the key's name. The server and first render draw Windows names, then the user's platform.
props.platform: "mac" | "windows" | "linux" — force a target platform instead of detecting it

props.keyName: string — optional modifier/key name to adapt ("mod", "meta", "alt", "ctrl", "shift")
props.platform: "mac" | "windows" | "linux" — force a target platform instead of detecting it

a11y: Use the <kbd> element: screen readers and search know it's a key.
Write modifier names out where symbols may not read well ("Ctrl" rather than "^"), or add aria-label="Command K" to a <kbd>⌘K</kbd> (screen readers pronounce "⌘" as "place of interest sign").
A shortcut hint doesn't replace aria-keyshortcuts on the control it triggers.
do: Use a kbd for keys people press: "Press / to search", shortcuts in a menu or tooltip, a hint in a search field (InputGroupAddon).
Use one kbd for a whole shortcut (⌘K), or one per key with a plus between them (Ctrl + Shift + P).
Adapt modifiers to the user's OS: ⌘ / ⌥ / ⇧ / ⌃ on macOS, Ctrl / Alt / Shift / Win on Windows, and Ctrl / Alt / Shift / Super on Linux (or use <Shortcut keys="Mod+K" /> / <Kbd keyName="mod" />).
Listen to event.code (physical key like 'KeyE') or use matchShortcut(event, 'Mod+E') rather than event.key === 'e' so hotkeys work across keyboard layouts and languages (e.g. Russian Cyrillic Cmd+У).
dont: Don't use a kbd for code or file names — use .ayy-mono or <code>.
Don't use it as a badge or a tag — use Badge.
Don't show shortcuts on touch-first screens, where there's no keyboard.
Don't hardcode Mac-only symbols (⌘) or Windows-only names (Ctrl) when targeting multiple operating systems.
Don't check event.key for letter shortcuts: on non-Latin keyboard layouts (e.g. Russian ЙЦУКЕН), event.key produces localized characters ('у' instead of 'e') and the hotkey fails silently.

Icons come from `npm i @hugeicons/core-free-icons`: import { Search01Icon } from "@hugeicons/core-free-icons". Plain HTML: paste the SVG with class="ayy-icon".

props.label: string — accessible name; without it the icon is decorative (aria-hidden)
props.strokeWidth: number — stroke width on the 24px grid (Hugeicons default 1.5)

a11y: Icons are decorative by default (aria-hidden): the text next to them carries the meaning.
When the icon is the only thing saying something (a status, a verified mark), give it a label: <Icon label="Deployed">, or role="img" + aria-label on the <svg>.
Icon-only buttons: aria-label goes on the button, the icon stays decorative.
Strokes use currentColor, so icons follow the theme and Windows High Contrast colours with no extra CSS.
do: Use an icon next to its text to help people recognise an action or item: buttons, menu items, list rows.
Use an icon with an accessible label for compact status where a word would be too long.
Import icons one by one from @hugeicons/core-free-icons; named imports tree-shake.
Let the component size icons inside buttons, menu items and alerts; use size for icons on their own.
Colour an icon through its text colour: .ayy-muted, or color: var(--ayy-color-success) on the <svg>.
Mark icons that point along the reading direction (arrows, chevrons, send, undo) directional so they mirror in RTL. Leave the rest alone: a clock or a check mark reads the same both ways.
dont: Don't use an icon for people and workspaces — use Avatar.
Don't use Icon for illustrations and logos — use an or your own SVG.
Don't rely on an icon when its meaning isn't obvious — write the word instead of (or next to) it.
Don't mix in another icon set. Hugeicons' 1.5px rounded stroke is part of the look.
Don't keep a fixed colour (color, fill or stroke set to a hex value) on an SVG you paste in: a black icon disappears in the dark theme.
Don't use colour as the only signal: pair a status icon with a label.

components.name: List
components.description: Rows of people, records, threads or settings: leading media (avatar, icon, icon tile), a title over a description, and trailing meta or a control. A link in the title makes the whole row clickable.

classes.ayy-list: Root <ul>. Rounded rows with a small gap between them.
classes.ayy-list--divided: Flush rows with hairlines between them: settings rows, records inside a card.
classes.ayy-list--compact: Tight rows without padding and a small icon: an icon checklist (plan perks, what's included, requirements). Rows here usually hold an Icon and plain text.
classes.ayy-list__item: The <li> row: a flex row of leading media, __content and trailing items, vertically centred. Everything but __content keeps its size.
classes.ayy-list__content: The column that holds __title and __description; it takes the free space and can shrink (add .ayy-truncate to cut long text).
classes.ayy-list__title: The row's main text, medium weight. Holds the __link when the row opens something.
classes.ayy-list__description: Supporting text under the title, muted.
classes.ayy-list__meta: Short trailing text: a time, a count, a size. Small, muted, tabular numbers.
classes.ayy-list__link: The <a> inside __title. Its ::after covers the row, so the whole row is one tab stop; other controls in the row stay clickable above it. The row gets a wash on hover, a ring on focus, and a stronger tint and heavier title with aria-current="page" (or "true").

default.looks: Rows of leading media, a medium-weight title over a muted description, and muted xs meta, with 12px padding and lg radius. divided: flush rows between hairlines; compact: tight icon rows.

hover.looks: A row with a __link gets a wash fill. Rows without one don't react.

pressed.none: No pressed look.

focus.looks: The ring goes around the whole row, inset by 2px.

disabled.none: Rows aren't disabled; leave the link out of a row that can't open, and disable controls inside it.

selected.looks: The row you're on: wash-hover fill and a semibold title, as the App shell's current link. Forced colours: Highlight. For multi-select rows put a Checkbox in the row.

error.none: No error look; show a failed load as an Alert in place of the list.

loading.none: No loading look; show Skeleton rows (circle plus two text lines) with aria-busy on the list.

sizes.density: Padding and sm text are fixed; row meta text follows data-density via --ayy-text-s; controls in rows follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container; titles and descriptions wrap, meta stays on one line.

components.js: listClass({ divided?, compact?, className? }) → string; listItemClass, listContentClass, listTitleClass, listDescriptionClass, listMetaClass, listLinkClass constants.

react.import: import { List, ListItem, ListContent, ListTitle, ListDescription, ListMeta, ListLink } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.compact: boolean — tight rows for an icon checklist.

a11y: It's a real list: screen readers announce how many rows there are.
One link per row, in the title, so a row is one tab stop with a meaningful name. Buttons and switches in the row are separate tab stops after it.
Mark the open row with aria-current="page" (it's a page) or "true" (a selection in a list-detail view); it gets a tint and a heavier title, not just colour.
A switch or checkbox in a settings row needs its label: make the title a <label for> pointing at it.
Avatars and icons in the leading slot are decorative when the title names the row.
do: Use a list for a feed of similar things people scan and open: conversations, notifications, files, members, search results.
Use List divided for settings: a title and description per row, the Switch or Button at the end.
Use List compact for a short checklist with an icon per row: plan perks, what's included, password rules.
Keep the same slots on every row: if one row has an avatar, they all do.
Put the time or count in ListMeta, and a status in a Badge at the end.
Cut long descriptions to one line with .ayy-truncate in inboxes and pickers.
dont: Don't use a list for data people compare across columns — use a Table.
Don't use it for the site or app navigation — use the App shell or Navbar.
Don't put two links in a row's title, or wrap the whole <li> in an <a>.

components.name: Swipe actions
components.description: A list row that slides sideways to show buttons underneath, as in phone mail and task apps: swipe toward the end for Done, toward the start for Snooze or Delete. Works with touch, pen and mouse, follows the reading direction, and keyboards reach the buttons with Tab.

classes.ayy-swipe: The row: clips its content and holds the trays. Vertical drags still scroll the page (touch-action: pan-y).
classes.ayy-swipe__content: What slides: the row's own content (often with .ayy-list__item). Opaque, with --ayy-swipe-bg (default the page colour) so the trays stay hidden under it.
classes.ayy-swipe__actions: A tray of buttons under the row, after the content in the DOM. Shows over the row while it holds keyboard focus.
classes.ayy-swipe__actions--start: At the inline start: revealed by swiping toward the inline end (right in English). One positive action (Done, Read).
classes.ayy-swipe__actions--end: At the inline end: revealed by swiping toward the inline start. Up to three (Pin, Snooze, Delete), the destructive one last.
classes.ayy-swipe__action: A <button> filling the tray's height: an icon over a short label, on a tint of its colour.

default.looks: The row as it is; its trays are hidden underneath until it slides.

hover.none: No hover look; swiping works with a mouse too, and Tab reaches the buttons.

pressed.none: No pressed look on the actions; they run at once.

focus.looks: Tabbing into a tray shows it over the row, and the action gets a ring inside its edge.

disabled.none: Don't offer an action that can't run; leave it out of the tray.

selected.none: Rows select through the list they're in (aria-selected on the item), not through the swipe.

error.none: If an action fails, close the tray and say so in a toast.

loading.none: Actions run at once (optimistic); undo through the toast.

open.looks: The row has slid to show the start tray (swiped toward the inline end) or the end tray.

dragging.looks: The row follows the finger with no transition.

components.description: Chronological list of events, milestones, or history with vertical connecting tracks, status markers, timestamps, and descriptions.

pressed.none: No pressed state on timeline items.

focus.none: Timeline items do not receive focus; place interactive elements like links or buttons inside content.

a11y: Rendered as an ordered list (<ol>) by default so screen readers announce the item count and sequence.
Timestamps use the semantic <time> element with tabular numbers for consistent alignment and screen reader comprehension.
Decorative markers and track lines are marked aria-hidden="true" to prevent screen reader noise; important status information should be in the title or body.
Active pulse rings are visual enhancements; screen readers receive the active status via text in the title, body, or an accessible badge.
Supports Windows High Contrast mode via @media (forced-colors: active) with system CanvasText, Canvas, and Highlight colors.
do: Use a timeline to show a chronological log or sequence of events: deploy history, shipment tracking, audit trails, activity feeds.
Use TimelineMarker pulse on the latest or currently active event in a running process.
Use Timeline alternate for milestones, company history, or changelogs on wide marketing or overview pages.
Include TimelineTime with a semantic timestamp so users can anchor events in time.
Keep markers consistent within a timeline: all dots, or all icons, or all avatars.
dont: Don't use a timeline for a multi-step user task with future steps — use Steps.
Don't use it for navigation or hierarchical page links — use Breadcrumb.
Don't wrap entire items in clickable links — place interactive links or buttons inside TimelineTitle or TimelineBody.
Don't hardcode colors on markers or lines; use semantic tokens or status badges.

Don't nest interactive controls in every cell — one trailing actions column is plenty.

default.looks: Responsive grid of surface cards with line borders, rest shadow, optional top media preview, header, body and hairline footer.

hover.looks: Card border turns line-hover and reveals .ayy-grid__actions--reveal.

pressed.none: No pressed look; clicking a selectable card or its checkbox toggles selection on release.

focus.looks: Reveals .ayy-grid__actions--reveal while any checkbox, button or menu trigger inside the card has keyboard focus.

disabled.none: Cards aren't disabled; disable the controls inside them.

selected.looks: Text-colour border plus a 1px ring and a 4% text tint over the surface. Forced colours: Highlight outline.

error.none: Show a failed load as an Alert with a retry instead of the grid.

loading.none: No loading look; render Skeleton cards in the grid layout with aria-busy on the container.

sizes.density: Card padding is fixed (16px, 12px when compact); checkboxes and action buttons inside follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container with auto-fitting columns at least --ayy-min wide (16rem default, 13rem compact).

components.js: gridClass({ compact?, className? }) → string; gridItemActionsClass({ reveal?, className? }) → string; gridWrapClass, gridToolbarClass, gridSelectAllClass, gridItemClass, gridMediaClass, gridHeaderClass, gridSelectClass, gridActionsClass, gridTitleClass, gridDescriptionClass, gridBodyClass, gridFooterClass constants; connectGrid(root, { onSelectionChange? }) wires select-all, card checkboxes, card-body click selection and Shift+click range selection (used by <ayy-grid>).

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-grid-wrap or .ayy-grid. Wires the .ayy-grid__select-all checkbox (including indeterminate state), each card's .ayy-grid__select checkbox, card-body click-to-select, and Shift+click range selection.

react.import: import { GridWrap, GridToolbar, GridSelectAll, Grid, GridItem, GridItemMedia, GridItemHeader, GridItemSelect, GridItemActions, GridItemTitle, GridItemDescription, GridItemBody, GridItemFooter } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.compact: boolean — denser cards and 13rem minimum column width

props.onSelectedChange: (selected: boolean) => void — toggles selection when the card body is clicked

props.reveal: boolean — reveal on card hover, focus-within or selection (stays visible on touch)

a11y: Each selectable card contains a native Checkbox in GridItemSelect with an aria-label naming the item ("Select Hero screenshot").
Selected cards carry aria-selected="true" and a 2px border (Highlight outline in High Contrast mode), never colour alone.
Per-card icon buttons and ⋯ DropdownMenu triggers carry an aria-label naming the item ("More actions for Hero screenshot").
GridItemActions with reveal uses opacity so controls remain in the Tab order and become visible on :focus-within.
do: Use Grid when items are browsed visually or as cards — media assets, screenshots, social media posts, projects and user records — and need multi-select and per-item actions like a Table.
Put GridItemSelect and GridItemActions inside GridItemMedia for visual cards (screenshots, media, social posts), or inside GridItemHeader for record cards (projects, users).
Provide a ⋯ DropdownMenu on each card for targeted secondary actions (Edit, Duplicate, Copy, Archive, Delete) and an ActionBar at the bottom for bulk actions on selected cards.
dont: Don't use Grid for static marketing feature tiles that aren't selectable records — use plain Cards in an .ayy-grid layout.
Don't use Grid for single-choice form inputs (like picking a pricing plan) — use ChoiceCard.
Don't hide the selection checkbox on selected cards.

components.name: Chart
components.description: Charts drawn by CSS with no library: columns (grouped or stacked), lines and areas, a ranked bar list and sparklines. Bars and ticks take --ayy-value (0–100), lines are SVG paths from chartPath(). Series colours are the chart tokens in order, so a chart library can match them.

classes.ayy-chart: Root, usually a <figure>. A grid of the plot, the labels, the legend and the data table.
classes.ayy-chart--stacked: A column's bars sit on top of each other; each bar's --ayy-value is its share of the top of the scale.
classes.ayy-chart--values: Print every bar's data-value above it (otherwise only on hover).
classes.ayy-chart__plot: The drawing area (aria-hidden="true"). Height from --ayy-chart-height (default 12rem). Holds ticks and either __bars or an __svg.
classes.ayy-chart__tick: A value line across the plot, its text the label in the gutter. --ayy-value places it: 0 is the floor, 100 the top. The gutter only appears when there are ticks.
classes.ayy-chart__bars: Row of columns filling the plot.
classes.ayy-chart__column: One label's bars, side by side (or stacked).
classes.ayy-chart__bar: A bar, fading toward its base (solid when stacked): --ayy-value is its height, data-value its text on hover. Its colour is chart-1, chart-2… by position in the column; --ayy-chart-color overrides.
classes.ayy-chart__svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" preserveAspectRatio="none"> stretched over the plot, for lines and areas. Mirrors in RTL.
classes.ayy-chart__series: <g> around one series' area and line. Coloured chart-1, chart-2… in order; --ayy-chart-color overrides.
classes.ayy-chart__series--compare: A comparison series (last period, a target): dashed, quiet, no fill.
classes.ayy-chart__line: <path> of the line, 2px whatever the stretch (vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke).
classes.ayy-chart__area: <path> of the area under the line: a 16% tint of the series colour, or fill="url(#…)" an __gradient in its series to fade out toward the floor (React does).
classes.ayy-chart__gradient: A <linearGradient x2="0" y2="1"> with two <stop>s, inside the series' <g> (in <defs>): its stops take the series colour, 32% at the top to none at the floor.
classes.ayy-chart__labels: The labels under the plot (aria-hidden="true"), one per column; under a line they spread from the first point to the last.
classes.ayy-chart__legend: List of the series, when there's more than one (aria-hidden="true" when a data table names them).
classes.ayy-chart__legend-item: A series name with its swatch, coloured in the same order as the series.
classes.ayy-chart__legend-item--compare: Legend entry for a comparison series: a dashed swatch.
classes.ayy-chart__swatch: The colour square in a legend item.
classes.ayy-bar-list: <ol> of ranked rows (top pages, sources) with the bar behind the text. Readable as it is.
classes.ayy-bar-list__item: A row; --ayy-value is the bar's length (100 = the largest). The bar fades along the row.
classes.ayy-bar-list__label: The row's name (or a link), cut with an ellipsis.
classes.ayy-sparkline: A small <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" preserveAspectRatio="none"> line with no axes, for a stat or a table cell. Uses __line and __area paths.

default.looks: Bars, lines or areas in --ayy-chart-1… in order, muted s labels, hairline ticks; the drawing is aria-hidden and the numbers live in a table.

hover.looks: Its bars mix 20% toward the text colour and show their data-value above them.

pressed.none: Not interactive.

focus.none: Not focusable; the data table carries the numbers.

disabled.none: Not interactive.

selected.none: No selected bar or series.

error.none: No error look; show an Alert in its place.

loading.none: Use a block Skeleton of the chart's height while data loads; bars grow from 0 when they appear.

sizes.density: The plot is --ayy-chart-height (12rem) tall; bar-list rows are at least the sm control height; a sparkline is 6rem × 1.75rem. Chart labels and legend text follow data-density via --ayy-text-s.
sizes.width: Fills its container; columns share the width (bars at most 2.5rem wide).

components.js: chartScale(values, { ticks?, min?, max? }) → { min, max, ticks } with a round top; chartPercent(value, max, min?) → 0–100 for --ayy-value; chartPath(values, { min?, max?, smooth? }) → { line, area } path data for the 0 0 100 100 box; chartColors(target?, count?) → resolved rgb() strings and chartTheme(target?) → { colors, text, muted, grid, surface, fontFamily } for canvas libraries (Chart.js, ECharts); chartClass({ stacked?, values?, className? }), chartSeriesClass({ compare?, className? }), chartLegendItemClass({ compare?, className? }) and part class constants.

react.import: import { BarChart, LineChart, Sparkline, BarList, TableChart } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

BarChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart"> with a plot of __column/__bar, labels, a legend and a visually hidden data table

props.label: string — what it shows ("Signups per day"); the data table's caption
props.showValues: boolean — print values above the bars
props.max: number — top of the scale; rounded up from the data if omitted
props.ticks: number of value lines, default 3; 0 for none
props.format: (value: number) => string — ticks, hover values and the table; default compact (1.2K)
props.legend: boolean — default: more than one series

LineChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart"> with an __svg of __series paths, labels, a legend and a visually hidden data table

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.series: { name, values: number[], color?, compare? }[] — compare draws a dashed comparison line
props.smooth: boolean, default true (monotone: never overshoots a point)

props.label: string — makes it role="img" with this name; without it the sparkline is aria-hidden

props.max: number — value of a full bar, default the largest

TableChart.renders: <div class="ayy-table-wrap"><table class="ayy-table"> with headers, swatches and numeric cells

props.label: string — what it shows; the table's caption
props.labels: string[] — one per row along the side
props.format: (value: number) => string — cell values; default compact (1.2K)

a11y: The drawing is aria-hidden. The numbers go in a table (React renders one with .ayy-sr-only; add a visible Table if people need to compare values), with a <caption> saying what the chart shows.
Don't rely on colour alone: a legend names the series in the same order, the comparison series is dashed, and a title or a Stat states the takeaway ("Up 12% on last week").
Series tokens keep 3:1 against every surface in every theme. In High Contrast bars and lines take system colours, alternating between CanvasText and Highlight.
A Sparkline with a label is an image with that name; give it the trend in words ("Revenue, last 14 days, up 12%").
do: Use a chart to show a trend or a comparison at a glance: signups per day, revenue against last month, traffic by source. Put it in a Card with the title and the key number (a Stat) above it.
Use a bar chart to compare amounts across a few categories or periods, a line chart for a trend over many points, a bar list for a ranking, a sparkline beside a number.
Colour series with the chart tokens in order (React does it). With a chart library, pass var(--ayy-chart-1)… (SVG) or chartColors() (canvas), and chartTheme() for its text, grid and tooltip.
Mark the previous period as a compare series instead of a second bright colour.
Keep the scale honest: bars start at 0; let chartScale() round the top.
dont: Don't use a chart when the exact numbers matter more than the shape — use a Table.
Don't use a pie or donut for parts of a whole — a Bar list or a stacked bar is easier to read.
Don't pick series colours from the status or accent tokens unless the colour means something (success for a goal line).
Don't draw more than six series; group the rest as Other.
Don't add a second chart library just for a simple bar or line — these cover dashboards. Reach for one (Recharts, Chart.js) for zoom, brushing or maps, themed with the tokens.
